resources.string: Hush %1$s · for Spotify on this phone
Ads play normally. Turn on to remove them.
Ad breaks are removed automatically, whether the phone is in use or locked.
Music volume is muted while an ad plays.
Audio ads are left alone. Ad servers are still blocked.
Allow notification access so Hush can tell when an ad starts.
Skipping is paused. Until it\'s back, ads are muted.
The DNS filter isn\'t running. Video ads may appear.
Spotify isn\'t installed on this phone.
Lets Hush see when Spotify starts an ad. Hush doesn\'t read your notifications.
Filters Spotify\'s traffic only. Other apps aren\'t affected.
Not installed. Needed to skip ads; without it, ads are muted.
Installed but not running. Open it and tap Start. Needed after every restart.
Running. Allow Hush to use it.
Shows the status and a Turn off button.
Keeps Hush working while the phone is locked.

Hush needs Shizuku to restart Spotify when an ad starts. Shizuku is a free, open-source app that lets apps use the system tools Android normally keeps for computers. Setup takes about two minutes, once.
Shizuku is ready. Hush will now skip ads.
From Google Play, or from its official GitHub page.
In About phone, tap Build number seven times.
In Shizuku, choose Start via Wireless debugging and follow its pairing steps. Pairing is needed only once.
On this Android version Shizuku is started from a computer with adb. Open Shizuku for the command.
Hush asks for this as soon as Shizuku is running.
Shizuku stops when the phone restarts. Open it and tap Start again; Hush reminds you if it has to mute an ad because of that.
Restarts Spotify in the background to drop the ad break. Music is back in a few seconds.
Silences the ad and turns the sound back on when it ends. Works without any setup.
Ads play. The DNS filter still runs if it\'s on.
Off. Use this instead of Spotify\'s timer, which is lost when an ad is skipped.
Pauses Spotify at the end of this song
Stops video ads and ad-related freezes using a local DNS filter for Spotify only.
View or edit the blocked domains.
Restarts Spotify now and checks that your music comes back.
Nothing yet. Ads that Hush handles appear here.
One rule per line: block, nxdomain, redirect <host>, ip <a.b.c.d> or upstream <a.b.c.d>. A rule also covers subdomains. Lines starting with # are comments.
The ad was removed, but playback didn\'t restart. Tap to open Spotify.
Skipping needs a one-time setup, about two minutes. Tap to start.
Shizuku stops when the phone restarts: open it and tap Start. Until then, ads are muted.
The DNS filter needs VPN permission.
One-time setup, about two minutes. Until then ads are muted.
Optional: pair Hush once and Shizuku isn\'t needed anymore, not even after a reboot.
Pair Hush with Wireless debugging again to keep skipping.
Wireless debugging is off. Turn it on and Hush resumes by itself.
Paused because Wireless debugging is off. Tap Resume.

To skip an ad, Hush restarts Spotify. Android allows that only to tools you approve once through Wireless debugging. Hush pairs with it by itself: no other app and no computer needed, and nothing leaves this phone.
Skipping is ready. Hush restarts Spotify by itself when an ad starts.
In About phone, tap Build number seven times.
Tap Pair. In Wireless debugging, turn it on, tap Pair device with pairing code, and type the code into Hush\'s notification.
Connect to Wi-Fi first. Wireless debugging works only on Wi-Fi (no internet needed).
Waiting for the code. In Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code.
Type the six-digit code into Hush\'s notification, or here.
One more switch on this phone
In Developer options, also turn on USB debugging (Security settings).
In Developer options, turn on Disable permission monitoring.
In Developer options, turn off Flyme payment protection.
In Developer options, turn on Allow ADB debugging in charge only mode.
Hush starts its helper and checks that it answers.
Turn on Wireless debugging; Hush then starts by itself.
Pairing gives Hush\'s helper only the few actions it needs (restart Spotify, keep it audible, bring back your app). You can remove Hush under Paired devices in Wireless debugging at any time.
In Wireless debugging, tap Pair device with pairing code.
Type the six-digit code shown in Settings.
Check the code in Settings and try again.
Keep the pairing code open in Settings and try again.
Hush will skip ads from now on.
Wireless debugging was turned off. Tap and Hush turns it back on. Until then, ads are muted.
Turn on Wireless debugging and Hush resumes by itself. Until then, ads are muted. Tap for the steps.
Skipping needs Wi-Fi (no internet needed). Hush resumes by itself when Wi-Fi is back. Until then, ads are muted.
Android forgot Hush\'s pairing. Tap to pair again (one code). Until then, ads are muted.
Hush couldn\'t start its helper. Tap to fix. Until then, ads are muted.
Off. After a reboot Hush asks you to tap once.
On. Hush turns Wireless debugging on for a moment after a reboot.
On. This phone keeps Hush ready with Wireless debugging off, so Hush leaves it off.
On. This phone stops Hush\'s helper when Wireless debugging is off, so Hush leaves it on.

After a reboot Android turns Wireless debugging off. With this on, Hush turns it on for a few seconds, starts its helper, and tests once whether this phone keeps the helper running with Wireless debugging off. If it does, Hush keeps it off; if not, Hush leaves it on. Hush never touches USB debugging or Developer options.
For bug reports: phone model, Android version and Hush\'s state only.
